passages.text: Then the LORD said to me: “Even if Moses and Samuel should stand before Me, My heart would not go out to this people. Send them from My presence, and let them go.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me.
He said, "Even if Moses stood before Me, I would not show favor to this people.
Even if Samuel stood before Me, I would not show favor to this people.
My heart is not with this people.
Send them away from My presence.
Let them go."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י אִם־ יַעֲמֹ֨ד מֹשֶׁ֤ה וּשְׁמוּאֵל֙ לְפָנַ֔י אֵ֥ין נַפְשִׁ֖י אֶל־ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה שַׁלַּ֥ח מֵֽעַל־ פָּנַ֖י וְיֵצֵֽאוּ׃

passages.text: If they ask you, ‘Where shall we go?’ you are to tell them that this is what the LORD says: ‘Those destined for death, to death; those destined for the sword, to the sword; those destined for famine, to famine; and those destined for captivity, to captivity.’
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Jeremiah.
The LORD gave Jeremiah a message for the people of Judah.
The LORD had rejected the people because of their sins.
If the people ask you, "Where shall we go?"
You must answer them.
This is what the LORD says.
Those who are destined for death will go to death.
Those who are destined for the sword will go to the sword.
Those who are destined for famine will go to famine.
Those who are destined for captivity will go to captivity.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֛ה כִּֽי־ יֹאמְר֥וּ אֵלֶ֖יךָ אָ֣נָה נֵצֵ֑א וְאָמַרְתָּ֨ אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר לַמָּ֤וֶת לַמָּ֙וֶת֙ וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר לַחֶ֙רֶב֙ לַחֶ֔רֶב וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר לָֽרָעָב֙ לָֽרָעָ֔ב וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר לַשְּׁבִ֖י לַשֶּֽׁבִי׃

passages.text: I will appoint over them four kinds of destroyers, declares the LORD: the sword to kill, the dogs to drag away, and the birds of the air and beasts of the earth to devour and destroy.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD declares judgment.
The LORD will appoint four kinds of destroyers over the people.
The sword will kill them.
The dogs will drag them away.
The birds of the air will devour them.
The beasts of the earth will devour and destroy them.
passages.original: וּפָקַדְתִּ֨י עֲלֵיהֶ֜ם אַרְבַּ֤ע מִשְׁפָּחוֹת֙ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה אֶת־ הַחֶ֣רֶב לַֽהֲרֹ֔ג וְאֶת־ הַכְּלָבִ֖ים לִסְחֹ֑ב וְאֶת־ ע֧וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֛יִם וְאֶת־ בֶּהֱמַ֥ת הָאָ֖רֶץ לֶאֱכֹ֥ל וּלְהַשְׁחִֽית׃

passages.text: I will make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth because of what Manasseh son of Hezekiah king of Judah did in Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks about the people of Judah.
The LORD will make these people a horror.
All the kingdoms of the earth will see them and be horrified.
The LORD will do this because of Manasseh.
Manasseh is the son of Hezekiah.
Manasseh was king of Judah.
Manasseh did evil things in Jerusalem.
Because of what Manasseh did, the LORD will bring this judgment.
passages.original: וּנְתַתִּ֣ים לִזְוָעָה לְכֹ֖ל מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָאָ֑רֶץ בִּ֠גְלַל מְנַשֶּׁ֤ה בֶן־ יְחִזְקִיָּ֙הוּ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה עַ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֖ה בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: Who will have pity on you, O Jerusalem? Who will mourn for you? Who will turn aside to ask about your welfare?
passages.sermon:
Jerusalem, you have turned away from the LORD.
You have rejected God.
You have chosen your own path.
Who will have pity on you?
Who will mourn for you?
Who will turn aside to ask about your well-being?
No one will care for you.
No one will comfort you.
No one will seek your peace.
passages.original: כִּ֠י מִֽי־ יַחְמֹ֤ל עָלַ֙יִךְ֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וּמִ֖י יָנ֣וּד לָ֑ךְ וּמִ֣י יָס֔וּר לִשְׁאֹ֥ל לְשָׁלֹ֖ם לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: You have forsaken Me, declares the LORD. You have turned your back. So I will stretch out My hand against you and I will destroy you; I am weary of showing compassion.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to Jerusalem.
The LORD says, “You have abandoned Me.
You have turned your back on Me.
I will raise My hand against you.
I will destroy you.
I am tired of showing mercy.”
passages.original: אַ֣תְּ נָטַ֥שְׁתְּ אֹתִ֛י נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֖ה אָח֣וֹר תֵּלֵ֑כִי וָאַ֨ט אֶת־ יָדִ֤י עָלַ֙יִךְ֙ וָֽאַשְׁחִיתֵ֔ךְ נִלְאֵ֖יתִי הִנָּחֵֽם׃

passages.text: I will scatter them with a winnowing fork at the gates of the land. I will bereave and destroy My people who have not turned from their ways.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about His people, Israel.
God says, “I will scatter My people.
I will use a winnowing fork.
I will do this at the gates of the land.
I will take away their children.
I will destroy My people.
They have not turned from their evil ways.
They have not repented.”
passages.original: וָאֶזְרֵ֥ם בְּמִזְרֶ֖ה בְּשַׁעֲרֵ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ שִׁכַּ֤לְתִּי אִבַּ֙דְתִּי֙ אֶת־ עַמִּ֔י מִדַּרְכֵיהֶ֖ם לוֹא־ שָֽׁבוּ׃

passages.text: I will make their widows more numerous than the sand of the sea. I will bring a destroyer at noon against the mothers of young men. I will suddenly bring upon them anguish and dismay.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD will make their widows very many.
Their widows will be more than the sand by the sea.
The LORD will send a destroyer at noon.
The destroyer will come against the mothers of young men.
The LORD will bring sudden anguish upon them.
The LORD will bring dismay upon them.
passages.original: עָֽצְמוּ־ לִ֤י אַלְמְנֹתָו֙ מֵח֣וֹל יַמִּ֔ים הֵבֵ֨אתִי לָהֶ֥ם עַל־ אֵ֛ם בָּח֖וּר שֹׁדֵ֣ד בַּֽצָּהֳרָ֑יִם הִפַּ֤לְתִּי עָלֶ֙יהָ֙ פִּתְאֹ֔ם עִ֖יר וּבֶהָלֽוֹת׃

passages.text: The mother of seven will grow faint; she will breathe her last breath. Her sun will set while it is still day; she will be disgraced and humiliated. And the rest I will put to the sword in the presence of their enemies,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks about His people who have not turned from their evil ways.
A mother has seven children.
This mother will become weak.
She will breathe her last breath.
Her sun will set while it is still day.
She will feel shame.
She will be humiliated.
The LORD will give the rest of her children to the sword.
Their enemies will see this happen.
The LORD has declared this.
passages.original: אֻמְלְלָ֞ה יֹלֶ֣דֶת הַשִּׁבְעָ֗ה נָפְחָ֥ה נַפְשָׁ֛הּ בָּאָה שִׁמְשָׁ֛הּ בְּעֹ֥ד יוֹמָ֖ם בּ֣וֹשָׁה וְחָפֵ֑רָה וּשְׁאֵֽרִיתָ֗ם לַחֶ֧רֶב אֶתֵּ֛ן לִפְנֵ֥י אֹיְבֵיהֶ֖ם נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Woe to me, my mother, that you have borne me, a man of strife and conflict in all the land. I have neither lent nor borrowed, yet everyone curses me.
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah speaks in this passage.
He is a prophet.
He feels deep sorrow.
He says, “Woe to me, my mother.”
He says this because his mother gave birth to him.
He describes himself as a man of strife.
He says he is a man of conflict.
He says this strife and conflict are in all the land.
He says, “I have not lent to anyone.”
He says, “No one has lent to me.”
He says, “Everyone curses me.”
passages.original: אֽוֹי־ לִ֣י אִמִּ֔י כִּ֣י יְלִדְתִּ֗נִי אִ֥ישׁ רִ֛יב וְאִ֥ישׁ מָד֖וֹן לְכָל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ לֹֽא־ נָשִׁ֥יתִי וְלֹא־ נָֽשׁוּ־ בִ֖י כֻּלֹּ֥ה מְקַלְלַֽונִי׃ס

passages.text: The LORD said: “Surely I will deliver you for a good purpose; surely I will intercede with your enemy in your time of trouble, in your time of distress.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke.
The LORD promised to act.
The LORD said He will deliver you.
He will deliver you for a good purpose.
He will help you in your time of trouble.
He will intercede with your enemy.
He will do this when you face distress.
passages.original: אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אִם־ לֹ֥א שָׁרוֹתִךָ לְט֑וֹב אִם־ ל֣וֹא׀ הִפְגַּ֣עְתִּֽי בְךָ֗ בְּעֵ֥ת־ רָעָ֛ה וּבְעֵ֥ת צָרָ֖ה אֶת־ הָאֹיֵֽב׃

passages.text: Can anyone smash iron— iron from the north—or bronze?
passages.sermon:
Iron is very strong.
Iron from the north is even stronger.
Bronze is also strong.
No one can break iron from the north or bronze.
passages.original: הֲיָרֹ֨עַ בַּרְזֶ֧ל׀ בַּרְזֶ֛ל מִצָּפ֖וֹן וּנְחֹֽשֶׁת׃

passages.text: Your wealth and your treasures I will give up as plunder, without charge for all your sins within all your borders.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to His people.
He said, “I will give your wealth to others.
I will hand over your treasures as plunder.
I will not ask for payment.
I do this because of all your sins.
You have sinned in every part of your land.”
passages.original: חֵילְךָ֧ וְאוֹצְרוֹתֶ֛יךָ לָבַ֥ז אֶתֵּ֖ן לֹ֣א בִמְחִ֑יר וּבְכָל־ חַטֹּאותֶ֖יךָ וּבְכָל־ גְּבוּלֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Then I will enslave you to your enemies in a land you do not know, for My anger will kindle a fire that will burn against you.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God says He will hand them over to their enemies.
God will send them to a land they do not know.
God’s anger burns against them.
God’s anger will become like a fire.
This fire will burn against them.
passages.original: וְהַֽעֲבַרְתִּי֙ אֶת־ אֹ֣יְבֶ֔יךָ בְּאֶ֖רֶץ לֹ֣א יָדָ֑עְתָּ כִּֽי־ אֵ֛שׁ קָדְחָ֥ה בְאַפִּ֖י עֲלֵיכֶ֥ם תּוּקָֽד׃ס

passages.text: You understand, O LORD; remember me and attend to me. Avenge me against my persecutors. In Your patience, do not take me away. Know that I endure reproach for Your honor.
passages.sermon:
The prophet Jeremiah speaks to the LORD.
Jeremiah knows that the LORD understands him.
Jeremiah asks the LORD to remember him.
Jeremiah asks the LORD to care for him.
Jeremiah asks the LORD to punish those who persecute him.
Jeremiah asks the LORD not to let him die while the LORD waits patiently.
Jeremiah tells the LORD that he suffers shame for the LORD’s sake.
passages.original: אַתָּ֧ה יָדַ֣עְתָּ יְהוָ֗ה זָכְרֵ֤נִי וּפָקְדֵ֙נִי֙ וְהִנָּ֤קֶם לִי֙ מֵרֹ֣דְפַ֔י אַל־ לְאֶ֥רֶךְ אַפְּךָ֖ תִּקָּחֵ֑נִי דַּ֕ע שְׂאֵתִ֥י עָלֶ֖יךָ חֶרְפָּֽה׃

passages.text: Your words were found, and I ate them. Your words became my joy and my heart’s delight. For I bear Your name, O LORD God of Hosts.
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah is a prophet of the LORD God of Hosts.
Jeremiah found the words of the LORD.
Jeremiah received these words.
Jeremiah accepted these words deeply, as if eating them.
The words of the LORD brought Jeremiah joy.
The words of the LORD made Jeremiah’s heart glad.
Jeremiah bears the name of the LORD God of Hosts.
The LORD God of Hosts is the God who commands heavenly armies.
Jeremiah belongs to the LORD God of Hosts.
passages.original: נִמְצְא֤וּ דְבָרֶ֙יךָ֙ וָאֹ֣כְלֵ֔ם וַיְהִ֤י דְבָרֶיךָ לִ֔י לְשָׂשׂ֖וֹן וּלְשִׂמְחַ֣ת לְבָבִ֑י כִּֽי־ נִקְרָ֤א שִׁמְךָ֙ עָלַ֔י יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י צְבָאֽוֹת׃ס

passages.text: I never sat with the band of revelers, nor did I celebrate with them. Because Your hand was on me, I sat alone, for You have filled me with indignation.
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah is speaking to the LORD.
Jeremiah did not join those who mock or make merry.
Jeremiah did not celebrate with them.
The LORD placed His hand on Jeremiah.
Because of this, Jeremiah sat alone.
The LORD filled Jeremiah with anger and indignation.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ יָשַׁ֥בְתִּי בְסוֹד־ מְשַׂחֲקִ֖ים וָֽאֶעְלֹ֑ז מִפְּנֵ֤י יָֽדְךָ֙ בָּדָ֣ד יָשַׁ֔בְתִּי כִּֽי־ זַ֖עַם מִלֵּאתָֽנִי׃ס

passages.text: Why is my pain unending, and my wound incurable, refusing to be healed? You have indeed become like a mirage to me— water that is not there.
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah is a prophet of God.
He speaks to the LORD God of Hosts.
Jeremiah asks a question.
He says, “Why does my pain never end?”
He says, “Why is my wound so severe?”
He says, “My wound will not heal.”
Jeremiah speaks to God.
He says, “You have become like a mirage to me.”
He says, “You are like water that is not there.”
passages.original: לָ֣מָּה הָיָ֤ה כְאֵבִי֙ נֶ֔צַח וּמַכָּתִ֖י אֲנוּשָׁ֑ה֙ מֵֽאֲנָה֙ הֵֽרָפֵ֔א הָי֨וֹ תִֽהְיֶ֥ה לִי֙ כְּמ֣וֹ אַכְזָ֔ב מַ֖יִם לֹ֥א נֶאֱמָֽנוּ׃ס

passages.text: Therefore this is what the LORD says: “If you return, I will restore you; you will stand in My presence. And if you speak words that are noble instead of worthless, you will be My spokesman. It is they who must turn to you, but you must not turn to them.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD says these words.
If you return to Me, I will restore you.
You will stand before Me.
If you speak what is precious and not what is worthless, you will be My mouth.
You will be My spokesman.
They must come back to you.
You must not go back to them.
passages.original: לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אִם־ תָּשׁ֤וּב וַאֲשִֽׁיבְךָ֙ לְפָנַ֣י תַּֽעֲמֹ֔ד וְאִם־ תּוֹצִ֥יא יָקָ֛ר מִזּוֹלֵ֖ל כְּפִ֣י תִֽהְיֶ֑ה יָשֻׁ֤בוּ הֵ֙מָּה֙ אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְאַתָּ֖ה לֹֽא־ תָשׁ֥וּב אֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Then I will make you a wall to this people, a fortified wall of bronze; they will fight against you but will not overcome you, for I am with you to save and deliver you, declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Jeremiah.
The LORD promised to protect Jeremiah.
The LORD said, "I will make you like a strong wall to these people.
This wall will be made of bronze.
The people will fight against you.
They will not defeat you.
I am with you.
I will save you.
I will deliver you.
This is what the LORD declares."
passages.original: וּנְתַתִּ֜יךָ לָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֗ה לְחוֹמַ֤ת נְחֹ֙שֶׁת֙ בְּצוּרָ֔ה וְנִלְחֲמ֥וּ אֵלֶ֖יךָ וְלֹא־ י֣וּכְלוּ לָ֑ךְ כִּֽי־ אִתְּךָ֥ אֲנִ֛י לְהוֹשִֽׁיעֲךָ֥ וּלְהַצִּילֶ֖ךָ נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: I will deliver you from the hand of the wicked and redeem you from the grasp of the ruthless.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to Jeremiah.
The LORD promises to act.
I will deliver you from the hand of wicked people.
I will redeem you from the grasp of ruthless people.
passages.original: וְהִצַּלְתִּ֖יךָ מִיַּ֣ד רָעִ֑ים וּפְדִתִ֖יךָ מִכַּ֥ף עָרִצִֽים׃פ
